question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,0]\times [-2,0]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=4{x}^{2}y+3{x}^{2}-xy-2x. $$ Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,-1]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{1}≈[$ $-0.444$ $]$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}y+3{x}^{2}-xy-2x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}y+3{x}^{2}-xy-2x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8xy+6x-y-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-x\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(8xy+6x-y-2) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}-x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(8xy+6x-y-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}-x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8y+6 & 8x-1 \\ 8x-1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}8y+6 & 8x-1 \\ 8x-1 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}8xy+6x-y-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with
${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}8y+6 & 8x-1 \\ 8x-1 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}8xy+6x-y-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}8(-1)+6 & 8(-1)-1 \\ 8(-1)-1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}8(-1)(-1)+6(-1)-(-1)-2 \\ 4(-1)^{2}-(-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-2 & -9 \\ -9 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-2)\cdot 0-(-9)\cdot (-9)}[\begin{aligned}0 & 9 \\ 9 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{81}[\begin{aligned}45 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-0.444 \\ -1.012\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
